newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Swissair says to open Bratislava route.
newsitem.headline: Swissair says to open Bratislava route.

text.p: Swiss national carrier Swissair said on Thursday it would open a regular service between Zurich and the Slovak capital Bratislava from March 30 this year.
The 10 weekly flights will be operated by the private Slovak carrier Tatra Air as regular Swissair flights with Swissair flight numbers, Swissair officials told a news conference.
The move opens Bratislava to Swissair's international carrier and booking network.

With Bratislava's renovated airport currently handling only 20 percent of its annual passenger capacity of two million passengers, the move is also expected to attract travellers who have been using the international airport in nearby Vienna.
Up to now, Tatra Air, jointly owned by Slovak shareholders and Swiss company Arfinnair, has been operating regular flights to Zurich under its own name.
The move will make Tatra Air the first post-communist carrier to operate under the Swissair network and is one of the few airlines with which the Swiss carrier has concluded such an agreement.
The service will be operated with Tatra Air's two 35-seat Saab 30 aircraft.
Tatra Air was founded in 1990 as a private airline and last year carried over 43,000 passengers on regular flights, a 43 percent increase over 1995.
